payload.text: Thirty-four, señor? You descend by twos while I climb by ones — this cannot meet. Twenty-five pesetas, and that is the last step my purse will take today. Shall we close it?
Let us be civilised: 26 P.

¡Primo, qué gusto verte otra vez! —Nando, abre la maleta— Mira: raras a sesenta y tres, épicas a ciento sesenta y dos, fresquitas del barrio. Y si traes comunes o poco comunes, te las compramos ahí mismo, sin rodeos. Pero decide rápido, que la maleta se vacía antes del mediodía, ¿eh?
Buenas tardes. Welcome. I see you carry the Guantería Antigua — a Salamanca piece, and my albums have a gap precisely there. I offer you 22 pesetas for it. A fair figure, I assure you.
Let us be civilised: 22 P.
Buenas tardes. You have read the books, bien. But books do not own the card; I do. El Gato de Lavapiés leaves my vault at 761 P. Those are my terms.
Thirty-eight? No, señor. I know every print run of that card, and it does not merit such a number. I move to 23 pesetas — a courtesy, not a bidding war. Shall we conclude?

¡Ay, primo, la maleta no tiene lista! Paco la mueve, Nando la cierra... Lo que hay, hay: raras a sesenta y tres, épicas a ciento sesenta y dos, del barrio que toque. Y comunes o poco comunes te las compramos al momento. Tú dime cuántas y cerramos, ¡rápido!

Let us be civilised: 23 P. That is my final word on the matter.

¡Eh, amigo, buenas! Paco y Nando, a tu servicio —

— y mira qué joya traemos: La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, pura pólvora y gloria. Setenta y tres, y sale de la maleta ahora mismo. Esta tarde ya no estamos aquí, te lo juro por mi hermano.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 63 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.
Cash changes nothing, señor. I am never in a hurry. El Gato de Lavapiés leaves this desk at 761 P. The terms stand as stated.
The market is not my concern, señor. I have shaved one peseta, and that is the whole of my movement: 760 P. The card waits in my vault either way.

¡Paco, cierra la maleta! Escucha, amigo: cincuenta y siete, y es la última palabra que sale de esta boca. Los de la mesa de al lado ya la quieren, pero tú nos caes mejor, qué le vamos a hacer. Dices que no y desaparecemos, sin rencor. ¿Trato?

Ay, buenos días, cariño! Come, sit a little, the sun is strong today. Have you eaten? Look here — this one is La Chulapa, very pretty, she finishes a page beautiful. For you, veintinueve, 29 P. My favourite card since years, hijo.

¡Anda, un lector! Paco, este sabe más que nosotros. Mira, sin humo, sin cuento: El Organillero, pieza fina, suena solo cuando lo abres... —y te lo dejamos en 4 primas. Cuatro, hermano. Pero decide ya, que el tren nos silba y la maleta se cierra sola.

You again. Palacio de Velázquez. Thirteen points. Rare, and you know it.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit, look. You have eaten today? Bueno. This one here, Plaza del Dos de Mayo — very pretty card, my favourite of the whole set. For you, twelve P. My Sundays here are forty years now, and still I love giving this one away.
What keeps us apart is your arithmetic, señor. Five pesetas from me: 755 P. The card has waited years; it can wait longer.

¡Eh, amigo, come, come! Paco here, that's my brother Nando — don't look at his face, look at the card! Noche de Movida, genuine, still warm from the press. Seventy-three pesos and it walks home with you. Tonight only, we leave at dawn. ¿Sí? Say sí, hombre!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando there — welcome to the suitcase! Look, look: La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, 73 primas, and don't blink. I swear on my mother, this is the last one left in all Madrid. No more exist. Touch it, feel it — history in your hands, eh?

¡Siete! Nando, que este regatea al revés, ¡hacia arriba! No, hermano: cuatro primas, las mismas cuatro, que ya te lo dejamos regalado y el Organillero vale más que la maleta entera. Venga, decide, que salimos en un minuto y el tren no espera ni a Rinconete. ¿Trato?

Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 65 P.
You repeat yourself, señor; I do not. Seven hundred fifty pesetas, and that is the whole of today's movement. The gato sleeps well in my vault.

¡Amigo! Paco here, Nando's already unzipping the case — look, look, San Francisco el Grande, the big dome, the real one. Beautiful, no? For you, because you came back and your money is honest: 187 P. Handshake now, we're late for a train already.
Oh, you're killing us. 172 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.
Thirteen. Same as before. I said it once.

¡Ay, sesenta! Nando, did you hear? He wounds us! — He wounds us, Paco, right here. Mira, amigo, for your face, for your good taste: sixty-four. Sixty-four and the card is yours, wrapped, kissed, gone before the lamps go out. ¿Sí? Say sí, hombre, the mule is already loaded!
Welcome, hijo! Look, Perrito con Abrigo, 12 P. Made for beginners. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

¡Seis! Paco, que este nos quiere arruinar con elegancia. No, hermano: El Organillero, cuatro primas, ni una menos ni una más. Es la pieza que llevamos, la que suena, la que vale. Cuatro. Dilo ya, que la maleta se cierra y el tren pita dos veces. ¿Trato, Lazarillo?

¡Cuarenta y nueve! Nando, cover my ears, I'm bleeding! Look, amigo — 60 P, final, beautiful, a gift from our mother's heart. But rápido, eh? The polic— the taxi, the taxi is outside, motor running, driver shouting. We go in one minute. Say sí now, or she rides away with us.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 56 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!

¡Ay, amigo, flattery like that and Nando's already blushing! Listen — the crew in the next stall has been circling this one all morning, hands in pockets, waiting. But we like you better, you come back, you shake honest. 163 P and it's yours before they look up. ¡Rápido, the train!

¡Ay, hijo, qué simpático eres! Mira, nine is a little thin for my favourite one. We say ten P and I am happy, you are happy, everybody goes home contento. Take it, and come back next Sunday to tell me how it looks in your album.

payload.text: Oh, you're killing us. 155 P.
Buenas. You arrive at a good hour. San Francisco el Grande, from my reserves — my terms are one hundred thirteen. I do not haggle before coffee.
Buenas tardes, señor. You come at a good moment. The Palacio de Velázquez — El Retiro, my beloved Retiro — I would take it off your hands for 22 P. A fair figure, I assure you.

Ay, cariño, qué bonito, un regalo para un amigo. But this little one, Perrito con Abrigo, stays at 12 P. A complete page makes your friend smile for years, hijo. Have you eaten today? Go see El Chato later, he trades straight.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? This one here, Vermut del Domingo — a beauty, I keep it for someone nice. For you, 29 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Hola, cariño! Very well, gracias — have you eaten yet? Let me see... I have the Bici de Reparto here, a nice little common, just what you need. Twelve P and it is yours, hijo. It will look lovely on your Madrid page.

¡Cinco! Nando, cierra la maleta, que este hombre tiene labia de Rinconete y bolsillo de señor. ¡Trato hecho, cinco primas! Toma El Organillero, hermano, trátalo bien, que suena solito de noche. Y si alguien pregunta... nunca nos viste. ¡Que el tren ya pita tres veces! ¡Adiós, Lazarillo!

Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 12 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

¡Eh, amigo, qué ojo tienes! Paco, abre la maleta — Nando, saca la joya. Noche de Movida, la carta que todos buscan y nadie encuentra. Setenta y tres primas y te la llevas hoy. Mañana ya no estamos aquí, te lo juro por mi hermano.

¡Amigo, you climb like a goat, we love it! But listen — the crew next door has their hands out already, they want this dome bad. We like you better, so: 149 P. That's the last word, Paco's packing the case. Yes or we walk. ¡El tren!
Oh, you're killing us. 66 P.

Ay, hijo, qué corazón tienes. But Perrito con Abrigo is 12 P, same as always. Your friend's page will be complete, and that joy lasts years. Have you eaten? Go see El Chato at half past nine, he trades straight, cariño.

¡Ay, amigo, no! The train, the crew, the case is zipped. Today it doesn't happen — but we love you, truly, no hard feelings, none. Paco says next time, Nando says next time louder. Keep climbing like that goat and Madrid will hear it. ¡Hasta pronto, friend! We run!

Oh, oh... 12 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

¡Cuarenta y nueve! Paco, agárrame que me caigo. Escucha, amigo — ayer mismo dejaron de imprimirla. Se acabó, no hay más, lo que queda en esta maleta es lo último del mundo. Sesenta y dos primas y te la pongo en la mano ahora mismo. Mañana ni nos buscas.
Oh, you're killing us. 58 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?

Ay, cariño, you repeat it like a little song. But Perrito con Abrigo is 12 P, the same today as yesterday. Your friend's page complete — that is worth more than the coins. Eat something, hijo. And pass by El Chato at half past nine.
Buenas tardes. You remember the lesson; good. El Gato de Lavapiés leaves this desk at 761 P. That is my term. Take your time considering it.

Ay, buenos días, cariño! Come, sit a little, the table does not bite. Have you eaten today? Look here — this one is Las Vistillas, very pretty page, my favourite. For you, veintinueve, 29 P. A good start for a collection, hijo.

Hola, cariño! Come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten? No? Ay, these young people. Look here — El Frutero de Argumosa, my favourite card, the man with the oranges. He has lived in this box since Tuesday. For you, five P. Qué te parece?

Hijo, enough of the same little song — I hear it, and it does not change me. Asking the same thing four times is not trading straight, and I notice. Perrito con Abrigo is 12 P. Take it or leave it with a smile, cariño. El Chato opens at half past nine.
Amigo! Noche de Movida, 73 P, a gift, a real gift!
